basis: Skin and nail keratinization abnormalities and persistent oral mucosal leukokeratosis define the disease; oral leukoplakia occurs in 30-79%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral mucosal leukokeratosis is explicitly part of the disease definition and occurs in 30-79%.

basis: COQ7-related CoQ10 deficiency presenting as motor neuropathy; muscle atrophy (5/6) and pes cavus (3/3) reflect denervation and secondary deformity, without established direct muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: atrophy in 5/6 and pes cavus in 3/3 are consequences of motor denervation; direct muscle or skeletal disease is not established.

basis: Brain tissue necrosis in the anterior cerebral artery territory; the definition establishes cerebral injury rather than intrinsic arterial disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: the artery identifies the infarct territory; intrinsic vessel disease or thrombosis is not established by this concept.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment and skeletal overgrowth define the syndrome. Strabismus occurs in 3/5 and gingival overgrowth in 1/2; the gingival estimate has limited sampling.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: persistent gingival overgrowth is direct gingival pathology, reported in 1/2 assessed patients; confidence is limited by sample size.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal overgrowth defines this overgrowth syndrome; accelerated skeletal maturation occurs in 80-99%, with scoliosis in 3/5.

basis: Ischemic pituitary necrosis causes hormone deficiencies. Anemia and visual-field defects are annotated 30-79%, but direct blood-organ or ocular injury is not established.

decisions.haematologic: none: normochromic anemia is annotated 30-79%, but does not establish direct marrow or blood-cell injury from pituitary necrosis.
decisions.ocular: none: visual-field defects are annotated 30-79%, but pituitary or chiasmal dysfunction does not establish direct injury to the eye or optic nerve.

basis: Defining eye, cognitive, hearing and dental defects; dental hypoplasia 80-99%. Cap omits renal proteinuria (80-99%)/bladder defects (30-79%) and cardiac septal defects (30-79%).

decisions.renal: none under the four-axis cap: proteinuria is annotated 80-99% and bladder diverticula 30-79%; defining dental malformations take the remaining slot.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dental hypoplasia is a defining structural defect affecting 80-99%; placed here because primary is limited to three axes.

basis: Severe neurodevelopmental disorder with movement abnormalities and seizures; strabismus affects ocular alignment in 1/2 assessed patients, with limited sampling.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus is persistent dysfunction of ocular alignment, reported in 1/2 assessed patients; the frequency estimate is uncertain.

basis: Upper thoracic myelomeningocele affects vertebral closure and spinal neural tissue; common neurogenic bladder is a separately diagnosed consequence of neural injury.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder is common (>80%) but is a separately diagnosed consequence of spinal denervation, rather than direct urinary-organ injury.

basis: Skeletal malformations, microcephaly/intellectual disability, deafness and cataract define the syndrome; cataract occupies the fourth slot because primary is capped at three.

decisions.ocular: involved: cataract is a defining diagnostic feature; placed here because primary is limited to three axes.
decisions.otologic: primary: deafness is an explicitly defining feature of the syndrome.

basis: Defined by external and middle-ear malformations causing conductive deafness, together with micrognathia, a congenital mandibular skeletal abnormality.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: micrognathia is an explicit defining mandibular skeletal malformation; primary classification does not require additional functional loss.
